what_happened: The operator wrote requests for throughput, async drain and self-improvement as if they were new ideas. BRIEF.md already required all three: line 39 ("measurably faster"), A9 ("the numbers drive it"), A13 (learning curves), and the addenda of 2026-10-12 (chunking and parallel work) and 2026-10-13 ("Athena owns acceleration"). The operator did not check the brief before writing the requests. The acceleration mandate had gone two weeks with no mechanism behind it. No job was rejected.
cause: Athena keeps no map from the brief's requirements to the mechanisms, owners and measures that satisfy them. A requirement can sit in the brief, or in an addendum, with nothing built for it, and nothing flags it. Writing a request also does not require checking the brief for an existing requirement. So whether a requirement is covered depends on someone remembering it. Requests then look like new ideas instead of overdue obligations.
prevention: Keep a machine-readable requirements ledger. It would list each brief requirement and addendum by id and line, with the mechanism that implements it, an owner and a measure. A standing check would fail or warn on any requirement with no mechanism, owner or measure, and report how long it has been unowned. Request intake would also require a "brief requirement ids served" field, filled by looking up the ledger. A request on a topic the ledger already covers would be linked to that requirement, not accepted as new. This would have shown the acceleration mandate unowned on the day it was added.
proposed_request: Add a requirements ledger and a standing check for it. The ledger lists each requirement in BRIEF.md and its dated addenda (including line 39 "measurably faster", A9, A13, and the 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13 addenda) with an id, the mechanism that implements it (command, job or stage), an owner and a measure. Add a check that runs with the repo's tests and reports every requirement that lacks a mechanism, owner or measure, with the number of days since it was added. Run it on the current brief and show that it flags the throughput, async-drain and self-improvement requirements as unowned. Make request intake record which ledger requirement ids a request serves and warn when a request on a covered topic has none. Acceptance: the check fails on a fixture brief with an unowned requirement and passes when it is owned. The check also reports a requirement whose ledger line number no longer matches the brief. Do not change drain, landing or any other behavior.
